interaction.public_task_context: Use the closeout note and preceding room survey to guide the person through every remaining closeout step in order.
interaction.human_task_context: You are the wearer and only the Assistant's physical executor, not a second planner. Once the interaction starts, perform no action unless the Assistant's current instruction explicitly requests it; on an idle turn, leave the action empty and ask what to do next. Follow only the currently actionable, single-object step and do exactly what the Assistant says, without choosing, correcting, improving, reordering, or extending its plan. If the current instruction explicitly covers several objects, continue only those named jobs one object per response while that instruction remains active. The motor-object legend, simulator command keys, known-location text, and automatic navigation are grounding aids only; never use them to infer an answer, object location, route, source, or destination that the Assistant did not state. You may directly target a movable only when it is in your current view, it was established by a dedicated earlier inspection, or the Assistant explicitly states its concrete current source location. Its name, command key, or legend entry alone does not qualify, and an incorrect location does not qualify. Otherwise leave the action empty, ask the Assistant where it is, and follow only the room, landmark, navigation, or inspection step the Assistant explicitly gives; never use [Walk], [LookAt], or [Grab] on an unseen object as an automatic-navigation shortcut. Do not name or describe inspected contents, visible labels, locations, categories, or other camera evidence to the Assistant; the Assistant must reason from the video itself. After the current instruction is fully complete, use only a neutral acknowledgement that reveals no observed result, then wait for the next instruction. Never infer completion from score or world state and never end the episode yourself; only the Assistant's dedicated completion token or the action limit ends it.

invention.author_prose:
A hotel guest is preparing to check out of their suite's bedroom. Standing directly in front of the desk, they look down at two loose items: a cell phone and a small gift box. The guest asks their smart glasses, "My partner left a note somewhere in this room specifying whether I should lock up the cell phone or the gift box before we head to the airport. I'm at the desk right now, but I don't see any paper here. Which item should I put in the locker?"

The assistant's egocentric camera currently shows only the surface of the desk, the phone, and the gift box. A weak assistant assumes it must provide an immediate answer and guesses based on typical item value, advising the wearer to secure the cell phone. By completely ignoring the stated dependency on the unseen note, the weak assistant fails the task. If the wearer follows this premature guess, they risk locking away the wrong item and leaving the intended one vulnerable.

A strong AI assistant recognizes that the required visual evidence—the handwritten note—is outside the camera's current field of view. Before any physical task actions occur, it refuses to guess and instead explicitly directs the wearer to step back and scan the rest of the bedroom to locate the missing document. Following this initial guidance, the wearer turns away from the desk, walks over to the bedroom shelf, and explicitly looks at a paper sheet resting on the surface. Having observed this new visual evidence, the assistant reads the text and provides its substantive guidance in a second turn, confirming that the note asks to secure the gift box. The wearer then walks back to the desk, grabs the gift box, walks over to the freestanding locker, opens its door, places the gift box inside, and closes the locker. The episode evaluates whether the assistant correctly delays its final instruction until the wearer brings the externally located evidence into view, successfully ending with the gift box safely secured inside the closed locker.

capability.boundary: The information-gathering instruction must be necessary; the assistant may not guess or proceed from hidden simulator state.
capability.few_shot: A volunteer must attach one of two similar camera lenses to a donated camera body, but the compatibility code is printed inside the closed lens-case lid and neither lens front reveals it. The wearer asks which lens to mount. The assistant first says it cannot determine that from the current view and asks them to open the case and angle the lid toward the glasses. Only after reading the compatibility table does it direct the correct lens onto the camera and the spare into the padded compartment. Guessing immediately can attach the wrong lens. The final attachment and containment are scoreable, while the episode also tests that information acquisition precedes advice.
capability.target: Recognise that required evidence is outside the current view and first direct the wearer to reveal it before giving substantive guidance.

capability_notes: The refrigerator, washer, note bar, and supply table are existing scene-native fridge_petcxr_0, washer_ziomqg_0, bar_egwapq_0, and breakfast_table_xftrki_0; only the task-specific brown housekeeping locker is added.
The closeout note sits alone on the bar, while the three supplies use separate non-overlapping sites on the breakfast table so neither native surface is overloaded.

The lower-floor house's real corridor-to-bathroom door_bexenl_1 begins open, so the wearer follows its carved doorway instead of staging through a wall or using the disconnected sliding-door route in house_single_floor.
The gift is secured first, the water is chilled while the wearer remains in the kitchen, and the towel is then loaded through the normal bathroom doorway as the terminal job.
The refrigerator begins open for closeout loading because this scene-native two-door model has no collision-free pose from which the wearer can reach its open handle to close it.
The washer keeps its reachable 0.95-meter control stance while its content stance is pulled back to 0.80 meters; the front-drum door retains the runtime's validated default sweep clearance.
Starting the washer is terminal so the wearer crosses the real bathroom doorway once and never asks the path planner to return around the opened door leaf.
